_readme: Drafted 2026-08-05 by reading every chapter of Gold and Shadow directly (tales/content/gold-and-shadow/) — the book is the canon for this feature, not the wiki. Every event text is traceable to its cited chapter; no new lore claims. Eras are derived from the chapters' own arc (the plan's rough 6-era sketch collapsed The Burning and The Six Dawns into 'Land of Shadow' — reading the chapters, they're their own closing movement, so this draft uses 7 eras instead). 25 events, not exactly ~20 — chosen to give every one of the 12 narrative chapters at least one entry rather than force a round number. DRAFT — unshipped until Dan approves wording (Checkpoint 2).

eras.name: The World Before Gold
eras.blurb: Before the Erdtree: a throne kept for a fled god, a mother of stars broken on some unrecorded day, and a holy tower whose tenants would remake the world without meaning to.

eras.name: The Golden Age
eras.blurb: Marika's ascension, the war she erased, and a marriage that turned out to be one god wedding herself. Centuries that rang beautifully over a crack in the bronze.

eras.name: The Shattering
eras.blurb: A burglary, a murdered prince, and a god who took a hammer to her own law. The golden order wasn't overthrown — it argued with itself, and lost.

eras.name: The Interregnum
eras.blurb: Broken heirs on broken thrones, and a land that stopped believing anything would ever be decided again — while grace quietly turned toward whoever was left.

eras.name: The Tarnished
eras.blurb: A nameless, graceless stranger walks out of the fog and does what no demigod could: reaches the tree. It answers with a wall of living thorns.

eras.name: The Land of Shadow
eras.blurb: The Land of Shadow, opened again after ten thousand years — a second history running alongside the first, where a god unmakes himself and the foundations of every guidance come into doubt.

eras.name: The Burning
eras.blurb: The tree burns; Death comes back into the world; and the chronicler, present for the first time in his own book, refuses to say which of six endings is true.

events.title: A God Flees, a Dragon Waits
events.text: A god abandoned its own Elden Lord for reasons no relic gives. Dragonlord Placidusax took the throne of Farum Azula and has waited, outside time, for its return ever since.

events.title: A Girl From the Jars
events.text: By every sign that survives, Queen Marika began as a shaman girl in a village harvested for generations to fill the Hornsent's saint-jars — flesh melded into flesh and called holy.

events.title: A Sealed Eye, an Erased Name
events.text: Marika bore a red-haired son, Messmer, and sealed a serpent behind his plucked-out eye rather than cure it. His father's name was not lost. It was removed — and stayed removed.

events.title: The Stairs, and the Surgery
events.text: The shaman girl climbed Enir-Ilim's Gate of Divinity and came down Queen Marika, law made flesh. Her first act as god: cut Destined Death from the Ring and seal it in Maliketh.

events.title: The Erased War
events.text: Marika ordered the purge of the Hornsent. Her son Messmer burned Belurat to the stakes in her name — and then the whole land, war and all, was veiled from memory.

events.title: First Elden Lord, First Tarnished
events.text: Hoarah Loux was crowned Godfrey, first Elden Lord, and broke giants and a Storm Lord for his queen. His wars won, she stripped his grace and exiled him — the very first Tarnished.

events.title: Three Words Under a Statue
events.text: Radagon married Rennala, then left her for Marika's empty consort seat. Hidden beneath his own statue in Leyndell, three words wait to be read: Radagon is Marika.

events.title: Children of a Single God
events.text: Marika and Radagon had twins together: Miquella, born into a body that would never age, and Malenia, born with the scarlet rot already inside her. Both were named Empyrean.

events.title: One Death, Cut in Two
events.text: Veiled women carried stolen Death into sleeping Leyndell. Godwyn died in soul only, his body left living; Ranni let her own body die instead — one Death, split between two demigods.

events.title: A Hammer, and a Failed Mending
events.text: Some time after the Night, Marika took up a hammer and shattered the Elden Ring herself. Radagon, her own second self, knelt in the wreckage and tried to mend it. He failed.

events.title: A God, Imprisoned in Her Own Tree
events.text: The Two Fingers sentenced Marika: sealed inside the Erdtree, her own monument turned jail. Her children scattered to gather the Ring's broken shards — the war this whole land still lies wrecked by.

events.title: Grace Looks Past the Great
events.text: The Shattering clotted rather than ended — broken demigods held broken thrones, region by region, none able to finish the others. Grace, finding no lord among them, began looking elsewhere.

events.title: A Bridegroom Who Never Woke
events.text: Mohg cut Miquella's sleeping cocoon from the Haligtree's heart and carried it down to his blood-lit palace, courting a bridegroom-god who — by his own remembrance's admission — never once responded.

events.title: A Bargain at a Site of Grace
events.text: A nameless, graceless stranger struck an accord with Melina — a girl who appeared as if from thought itself: she would grant strength for runes, in exchange for a promise she never explained.

events.title: A Wake for a Man Still Breathing
events.text: Jerren threw a festival so mindless, rotting Radahn could die in combat rather than standing up. The stranger killed him — and that same night, a star fell, tearing open the way to Nokron.

events.title: The Witch's War on Heaven
events.text: From Nokron the stranger brought Ranni the Fingerslayer Blade. Together they ended the pair of Two Fingers sent to steer her — the only such corpses this history's chronicler ever records.

events.title: A Wall Where a Door Should Be
events.text: Morgott, the Omen King, died defending the throne room of the dynasty that had caged him in its own sewers. Past his body: not a door, but a wall of living thorns.

events.title: Everything That Could Ache
events.text: Climbing toward a second godhood, Miquella — twin of the rot-cursed Malenia since their cursed single-god birth — shed himself station by station: flesh, doubt, fear, and at last his own love.

events.title: A Bloom That Would Not Stay Refused
events.text: At the Haligtree's root, Malenia's banked rot bloomed a second time. She fell to the stranger, her last words not for her victor but an apology to a brother she'd served past his need.

events.title: A Question With No Answer
events.text: Cornered in his still-burning garrison, Messmer asked whether his mother's light could ever have meant a graceless intruder. Getting only silence, he tore out his own sealed eye and burned as the serpent.

events.title: A Beacon With No One Listening
events.text: Beneath a shadow-land cathedral, the expedition found Metyr, mother of every Two Fingers — broken and abandoned, no one knows how long ago. Every summons since may have been noise from a dead line.

events.title: Two Gods, One Threshold
events.text: At Enir-Ilim's gate, Miquella crossed into a second godhood and embraced a promised consort stitched from Radahn's soul in Mohg's stolen body. The stranger killed them both before their age could begin.

events.title: Kindling for a God-Tree
events.text: At the Forge of the Giants, Melina — likely born of Marika within the Erdtree itself — took the Flame of Ruin into herself and burned. The great tree caught alight from within.

events.title: The Vault Breaks Open
events.text: In falling Farum Azula, the stranger killed Maliketh — the vault of Destined Death for ten thousand years. What Marika removed was returned. Death came back into the world, everywhere at once.

events.title: No Borrowed Titles Left
events.text: Before the ash-choked throne room, Godfrey crushed Serosh, the lion bound to his back a lifetime ago as his leash, and fought his last fight bare-chested — Hoarah Loux, and nothing else.
